title: FEASTA: A Flexible and Efficient Accelerator for Sparse Tensor Algebra in Machine Learning
problem: General-purpose processors (GPU, CPU) inefficiently handle unstructured sparse tensor algebra due to hardware underutilization. Dedicated sparse accelerators optimized for specific tasks cannot effectively support diverse SpTA workloads with different dataflows and sparsity patterns.
motivation: Sparse tensor algebra is increasingly important in machine learning but demands specialized processing to overcome inefficiencies in existing hardware.
method: FEASTA uses three-level hierarchical design: (1) dataflow abstraction applying Einstein Summation on sparse fiber trees to model SpTA execution as fiber tree join/merge operations, (2) a general SpTA ISA with distinct instruction types for dense and sparse data, and (3) an instruction-driven architecture with configurable high-performance function units supporting the flexible ISA.
key_novelty: Unified modeling of diverse sparse tensor algebra tasks via Einstein Summation on fiber tree structures, enabling a single flexible architecture to support varying sparsity patterns and dataflows.
contributions: Fiber tree dataflow abstraction with Einstein Summation for uniform sparse tensor operation modeling
General-purpose sparse tensor algebra ISA with dense/sparse instruction types
Configurable hardware architecture with specialized function units
Demonstrates 5.40× energy efficiency vs GPU and 1.47-3.19× speedup vs specialized accelerators

metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 5.40× geomean energy efficiency vs GPU; 1.69-12.70× energy efficiency over existing architectures
metrics.speedup: 1.47× vs sparse matrix accelerator; 3.19× vs CPU extension

primary_theme: Unified sparse tensor accelerator with fiber tree dataflow
